messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT detected: elevated error rate on inference pool 'dedicated-gpu-3' (kv-cache service). alert_id=KB-9873, severity=high, triggered_by=rate/error_spike, metric=kv_cache_miss_ratio, value=0.62, baseline=0.04
oncall-dan: paging @oncall-dan — got the page, jumping in now. what's the impact?
sre-ana: perf dashboards show a sudden spike in per-token latency and 5xxs starting at 12:34 UTC. KV cache size exploded from ~1.2GB to 78GB on that pool, evictions thrashing.
eng-maya: hmm that smells like cache reuse gone wrong. recent rollout changed continuous-batching + kv reuse heuristics last night.
eng-olivia: confirmed — we pushed batch-routing v2 at 03:12 UTC yesterday which enabled aggressive prefix caching and reuse across requests.
support-jake: we have 3 active customer alerts, one says "responses returning content from other requests" — possible cross-request leakage.
oncall-dan: ok mitigation plan: 1) disable kv_reuse on the pool, 2) limit batch size to 1 for affected nodes, 3) scale down concurrency. can we do 1 now?
eng-maya: I can flip the flag remotely on the control plane, targetting dedicated-gpu-3 only. hotfix config: 
```
service.pool.dedicated-gpu-3.kv_cache_reuse: false
service.pool.dedicated-gpu-3.continuous_batch.max_batch_size: 1
```
apply in 30s?
sre-ana: apply now and watch for regressions. watchlist: kv_cache_total_bytes, token_latency_p95, model-errors-5xx.
oncall-dan: go for it.
deploy-bot: starting rollout of config change to pool dedicated-gpu-3 (user=eng-maya, id=deploy-7783)
eng-olivia: pushing logs from replica-7: seeing negative seq offsets and repeated KV key collisions in the debug trace: 
```
KVCache::get(key=conv-usr-12345, seq=102) -> stored_seq=98 -> mismatch -> returning stale value
KVCache::put(key=conv-usr-12345, seq=103)
```
support-jake: customer excerpt: "we got part of another user's assistant reply in our session" — customer is on a private Dedicated instance.
sre-ana: 12:39 UTC config change took effect. immediate drop in cache size to ~2.1GB and 5xxs decreased to baseline within ~60s.
oncall-dan: good. any sign of data loss or permanent corruption?
eng-olivia: logs show stale seq offsets were the root cause — cache keying didn't include request-level seq offset for continuation tokens in certain quantized kernels. When reuse=True, later requests could pick a matching key with mismatched seq range.
eng-maya: follow on: the continuous-batching router was normalizing prefix keys too aggressively — lost the shard offset suffix. Patch incoming.
pm-raj: need a short customer-facing note. support, can you triage impacted customers and classify severity?
support-jake: triaging now: 4 customers impacted, 2 with PII risk flagged (responses contained small user-specific completions). initiated emails and temporary rate-limits.
oncall-dan: who owns the postmortem and next steps? keep this thread for on-call handoff in 30m.
sre-ana: immediate remediation: kv_reuse disabled pool-wide, batch_size limited, autoscaler paused for the pool to avoid spinning more nodes. Hotfix diff: 
```diff
- kv_cache_reuse: true
+ kv_cache_reuse: false
- continuous_batch.key_normalization: aggressive
+ continuous_batch.key_normalization: conservative_with_seq
```
eng-maya: patch PR opened (GH #4521) to include seq in cache key and add strict validation in KV fetch paths. unit tests added for seq mismatch case.
eng-olivia: also adding a runtime guard that zeroes cache lookup if request has user-session-flag=private. defensive for private instances.
pm-raj: ETA for safe re-enable?
eng-maya: need full integration tests and a canary rollout. estimate 48 hours for tests + 6hr canary.
sre-ana: operational follow-ups: 1) run a sweep for other pools to detect similar config drift 2) add alert for sudden kv_cache_total_bytes growth 3) add checksum/seq validation metric for cache hits (flag mismatches).
oncall-dan: handoff: I'm on in 30m, @sre-ana will be primary until then. please put any new findings here.
support-jake: customers notified; CS escalations created: CS-1209, CS-1210.
eng-olivia: one more log snippet from a canary node showing how cross-request leakage happened: 
```
Request A: prompt="Order status for #1001", seq_start=50
Request B: prompt="Private note: SSN 123-45-6789", seq_start=12
Batching combined, kv key normalized to "conv-Order" -> reused value from Request B for A
```
sre-ana: note for postmortem: blame chain: config rollout (aggressive key normalization) -> missing seq in key -> reuse=True -> cross-request leakage -> cache blowup due to unseen churn -> perf cliff and 5xxs.
eng-maya: I'll add a safety toggle to force per-request namespaces for sensitive sessions.
pm-raj: create postmortem ticket and link to customers and timeline. assign to eng-maya + sre-ana.
oncall-dan: thanks. leaving this thread open for the handoff. if anything urgent, ping me.
sre-ana: summary for handover: incident resolved to low — root cause identified as kv key normalization bug combined with kv_reuse semantics. hotfix applied (reuse disabled + batch limit). customers notified. next: PR + tests, canary, alerting.
eng-maya: pushed PR to staging. running integration now. will update.
eng-olivia: thumbs on logs — no more cross-request examples after the hotfix.
support-jake: closing customer-facing loop, awaiting confirmation from 2 affected customers.
oncall-dan: thanks everyone. we'll run a full postmortem and include mitigations, post-incident review scheduled for tomorrow 16:00 UTC.
incident-bot: incident KB-9873 status changed: mitigated -> postmortem_scheduled (owner=eng-maya, reviewer=sre-ana, meeting=2026-03-16T16:00:00Z)
